Article Title: 'U-turn in a week': DMK slams Vijay over delimitation stance after Amit Shah meeting
Article Text:
The Stalin-led party accuses Vijay of taking 'U-turn' after meeting Amit Shah

NEW DELHI: The MK Stalin-led Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam on Thursday launched a sharp attack on Tamil Nadu chief minister C Vijay Joseph, accusing him of taking a "U-turn" on the issue of delimitation.The DMK 's criticism came after Vijay met Union home minister Amit Shah in Tamil Nadu on Thursday.Taking to social media, the DMK IT cell alleged that Vijay, who had earlier taken a strong stand against the Centre and Amit Shah over the issue of delimitation, had now changed his position.The party wrote, "Chief minister Vijay, who took a firm stand against Amit Shah on the issue of delimitation. Chief Minister Vijay, who, in the very same week that a resolution was passed to not increase the current number of 543 MPs, changed his stance."In another post, the DMK said, "Chief Minister Vijay has done a U-turn in a week on the constituency redrawing issue! Is this the same person who called Tamil Nadu's supporters of constituency redrawing the 'eight-footers'?"The party also took a veiled jibe at TVK allies in state, "Will the parties in the alliance question the duplicity in this double game by Thavega? Or will they also give a nod to this?"The attack came on a day Amit Shah chaired the 31st meeting of the Southern Zonal Council in Chengalpet, Tamil Nadu, bringing together representatives of five states and three Union territories to discuss issues concerning the Centre and the southern region.The meeting was held at the Taj Fisherman's Cove hotel in Kovalam and was hosted by the Tamil Nadu government. Chief ministers and senior representatives from the member states and Union territories attended the meeting, according to the ministry of home affairs.
Article Summary: Stalin-led party accuses Vijay of taking 'U-turn' after meeting Amit Shah. The DMK IT cell alleged that Vijay, who had earlier taken a strong stand against the Centre and Amit Shah over the issue of delimitation, had now changed his position.

Article Title: 'We fought wars with Pakistan too, but China will be India's main competitor': Ex-Army chief
Article Text:
General MM Naravane (Retd) on China and Pakistan

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Former Army chief General MM Naravane (Retired) on Thursday described China as India's "main competitor" in the years ahead, despite India having fought wars with both China and Pakistan."Pakistan and China are a totally different ballgame. We have fought wars with both of them. We have unsettled borders. So they will always remain on our radar as a threat, as a challenge," PTI quoted Naravane as saying at a book launch event in New Delhi.However, he distinguished between the two, saying India's immediate focus on Pakistan was driven largely by the continuing threat of terrorism, while describing China as a "competitor" rather than an "enemy." He emphasised that he had "purposely" used the term "competitor" for China."We have fought major wars with Pakistan, and because of their continued support to terrorism, our attention is towards our western borders. But I think we are very clear that in the long term and in the years to come, China is going to be our main competitor. And I purposely use the word competitor and not enemy," Naravane said.Naravane, who was Chief of Army Staff during the 2020 Ladakh clashes with China and led India's response, further stated that the two countries would be competitors across multiple domains, including politics, economics, trade and military affairs."They are going to be our main competitor in all fields. Political, economic, trade, and of course military also. And wherever there is competition, there is always a little bit of conflict," the retired Army general observed.He emphasised that India should seek to manage such differences through dialogue and diplomatic mechanisms rather than resorting to force."It is up to us to try to resolve those conflicts, those differences, through the mechanisms of talks, dialogues. And taking recourse to the use of force should always be the last priority," he said.However, he also stressed that India must maintain credible military preparedness to deter any potential misadventure."There comes a moment when you realise that this is not going to happen. And therefore, you have to have a strong deterrence. That is why the armed forces have to be ready at all times. You have to have a strong deterrence to stop anybody from taking recourse to the use of force or any misadventure," he remarked.
Article Summary: Former Army chief describes China as India's "main competitor" despite India having fought wars with both China and Pakistan. He distinguished between the two, saying India's immediate focus on Pakistan was driven largely by the continuing threat of terrorism. He emphasised that he had "purposely" used the term "competitor" for China.

Article Title: Decide on Dara Singh's remission plea or we will: SC to Odisha govt
Article Text:
Singh was part of a mob which set fire to Australian missionary Graham Staines's vehicle in 1999, killing him and his two sons, Philip (10) and Timothy (6), in Keonjhar, Odisha..

NEW DELHI: "Don't try to dodge us" was the terse warning Supreme Court issued to Odisha govt, which has been skirting the issue of Dara Singh 's remission plea over the last few months and refrained from revealing its stand to the court on Wednesday."You take a decision, whichever way you want. If you do not take a decision, then we will," the bench told state govt, posting hearing for Sept 2.Singh was part of a mob which set fire to Australian missionary Graham Staines's vehicle in 1999, killing him and his two sons, Philip (10) and Timothy (6), in Keonjhar, Odisha. Sentenced to death, later commuted to life term , Singh has been in jail for 26 years.A bench of Justices ­Manoj Misra and Vijay Bishnoi expressed its anguish over State Sentence Review Board not having made a decision yet, noting that hearing in the case has been adjourned multiple times to allow the state to take a call in the matter.Appearing for the state, advocate P V Yogeswaran placed before the bench a letter written by the prison authority stating that it had not received a report from district jail, Keonjhar.But the bench was not convinced and said, “We are not concerned about who is communicating what. We cannot tolerate this avoidance of decision.”Singh was sentenced to death by a trial court in 2003. In 2005, Odisha high court commuted death penalty to life imprisonment, which was confirmed by ­SC in 2011.The court said, “This matter has been adjourned time and again to enable the respondents to take a decision on the plea of remission of sentence awarded to the petitioner who is incarcerated for a period exceeding 26 years. It appears that when the matter was adjourned last, the State Sentence Review Board was in the process of taking a decision on the petitioner’s plea. Based on that, the matter was adjourned. Today, the learned counsel for the respondent has placed before us a letter of the Directorate of Prison and Correctional Services addressed to the counsel, wherein he stated that the report from the district jail, Keonjhar, is yet to be received. We are not informed of the sentence review board’s decision. List this matter on 2 Sept. The review board should take apprise us of their decision.”
Article Summary: Dara Singh was part of a mob which set fire to Australian missionary Graham Staines's vehicle in 1999, killing him and his two sons, Philip (10) and Timothy (6), in Keonjhar, Odisha. Sentenced to death, later commuted to life term, Singh has been in jail for 26 years.

Article Title: Battle for UP's 'Aadhi Aabadi': Why parties are wooing women voters like never before ahead of 2027 polls
Article Text:
Why UP's 'Aadhi Aabadi' matters more than ever in the 2027 election

Why women voters matter

How parties are wooing women voters

Congress's another shot at wooing women voters

Women are voting more, but are they voting as one bloc?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh elections have traditionally been about the caste arithmetic: counting Yadavs, non-Yadav OBCs, Dalits, Brahmins and Muslims. But ahead of the 2027 battle, there is another constituency the parties simply cannot afford to ignore: the women voters - who transcend the caste divide.Every election cycle, the same questions return: Can the BJP retain its non-Yadav OBC votes? Will Akhilesh Yadav manage to woo Brahmins and Dalits? Which side will the Jatav voters pick? Will Mayawati be able to rally all Dalits behind her BSP? And so on.This time around, while the caste questions remain, the battle will also be for the support of Uttar Pradesh's 'Aadhi Aabadi' - the women voters who have proved to be game changers, election after election in many other states.When Uttar Pradesh votes in 2027 to elect a new assembly, the state's 6,09,09,525 female voters, who constitute 45.46% of the total electorate, will hold considerable sway over the fortunes of the political contenders.That explains why Yogi Adityanath and Akhilesh Yadav, the two key challengers, are leaving no stone unturned to bring women into their fold. Congress, too, is preparing to step up its outreach as the electoral battle gathers pace.Let's rewind to 2007. In the 2007 UP assembly election, the female turnout in the state was under 42%, less than the male turnout of 49.35%.But this changed five years later. In 2012, Uttar Pradesh had around 5.72 crore registered women voters, of whom 3.45 crore cast their ballots. Thus, the female turnout increased to around 60.3%, surpassing that of males at about 58.7%.By the 2017 assembly election, the number of registered women voters had gone up to 6.46 crore. More than 4.09 crore women voted, and female turnout climbed to around 63.4% while the men lagged at 59%.In 2022, Uttar Pradesh had around 7.02 crore women electors, out of which more than 4.36 crore voted. Female turnout stood at around 62.2%, once again higher than that among men, which stood at around 59.6%.So, between 2012 and 2022 alone, the state added nearly 1.3 crore women to its electoral rolls. But what may be more important for political parties is the fact that 2012 elections onwards women outvoted men in all assembly elections in the state. The 2024 Lok Sabha election was no different.In Uttar Pradesh, 57.22% of women electors turned out to vote in the 2024 general elections, compared to 56.46% of men. The overall turnout was lower than in the recent assembly elections, but women still maintained their lead.And it’s not just UP. Parties cannot ignore the decisive role women voters have played in assembly elections in Bihar, Maharashtra, West Bengal, Madhya Pradesh and Jharkhand.Ahead of the assembly election in Madhya Pradesh, the Shivraj Singh Chouhan government rolled out the 'Ladli Behna' programme, a monthly cash assistance scheme under which money was transferred directly into women's accounts. By the time Madhya Pradesh voted, the scheme covered more than a crore women. BJP won 163 of the 230 seats. 'Ladli Behna' quickly became one of the key takeaways from the election.Maharashtra also introduced its own version: the 'Ladki Bahin' programme. And then Bihar happened. The 2025 assembly election recorded a female turnout of 71.6%. Male turnout was 62.8%. The NDA went on to win a huge majority.Financial doles under DBT (Direct Benefit Transfer) no longer make news. If the elections are round the corner, they are a given. What makes news is the amount of dole.So, when some media reports suggested that the Yogi Adityanath government was considering a dole of Rs 50,000 for women ahead of elections - Rs 20,000 now and Rs 30,000 after its return to power - Akhilesh Yadav lost no time to dish out a pre-election offer to counter the BJP. “We will start with Rs 40,000 and increase it every year,” the SP chief wrote in a post on X while questioning the BJP’s intent and alleging that the BJP was distributing "the earnings of its sins. "Akhilesh simultaneously launched a broadside against the BJP and alleged that the party has been left with "nothing but money" to win the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. “The religious women of UP will never accept the ill-gotten money of the BJP,” the SP chief wrote. He also tried to discredit the BJP and claimed that the party was not keeping its promise of giving the announced doles to women in other states where it governed."The BJP's corrupt government has eaten up Rs 5 lakh belonging to women over the last 10 years and is now serving the jumla of giving only Rs 20,000. Rs 20,000 is only four per cent of Rs 5 lakh, which means these BJP people have swallowed 96 per cent of women's share," he alleged.BJP Uttar Pradesh vice-president Neeraj Singh hit back at Akhilesh, saying his party has made no such announcement and accused the SP chief of making a "deceptive" promise to give Rs 40,000 to women."Whenever the BJP provides benefits under its schemes to eligible people, the important thing is that the money reaches those who are entitled to it. The distribution system is also very transparent, and this has been the BJP's track record," the BJP leader claimed.On the SP's promise of Rs 40,000 annually to women, Singh said it was "only a deception" and alleged that the party had used a similar tactic before the 2024 Lok Sabha elections.But while the BJP questions Akhilesh Yadav’s sincerity, it perhaps realises that the SP chief has raised the bar and also the expectation of women in the state by announcing a dole of Rs 40,000, and this announcement may influence whatever dole the ruling party eventually decides.Akhilesh may have scored some brownie points here, but the fact remains that the SP chief faces a tough challenge from the BJP in UP. Chief minister Yogi Adityanath has been in a relentless pursuit of women voters, announcing a string of programmes for them at regular intervals.In March, Yogi Adityanath distributed smartphones to 69,804 Anganwadi workers and supervisors, over two lakh growth monitoring devices, and appointment letters to 18,440 Anganwadi workers and helpers. Addressing the gathering, he said, "If the newborn is well-nourished and the mother is healthy, the future of India will be strong."In April, the Uttar Pradesh government launched a one-of-its-kind scheme titled 'Safe Mobility Program,' centred around employment generation for female members of Self-Help Groups (SHGs). Under the programme, an army of female e-rickshaw pilots will be trained across the state to ensure safe, accessible, and dignified transportation for girls and women travelling to schools, workplaces, and other essential destinations.From April 16 to 20, the Yogi government ran a five-day special campaign under the Nari Shakti Vandan Abhiyan to turn schools into active centres of women empowerment, focusing on building confidence, leadership qualities, and awareness among girl students.In another move to support and prop up 'naari shakti', the Uttar Pradesh government directed sugarcane co-operative societies in the state to allocate free spaces to women from Self Help Groups (SHGs) to set up their shops. The idea was to encourage women from SHGs to start ‘Prerna canteens’ from here, displaying and selling their products.These are some examples that showcase how Yogi Adityanath has been mindful of the power of women voters in the 2027 battle and has been working to reach out to them through his welfare measures.BJP and Samajwadi Party are not the only parties to target this demographic. Congress had, in fact, put women at the centre of its Uttar Pradesh campaign much before the current race over cash transfers began. In 2022, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, who was the general secretary of the All India Congress Committee (AICC) in charge of Uttar Pradesh back then, led the party's 'Ladki Hoon, Lad Sakti Hoon' campaign. The party took a bold gamble by promising to give 40% of assembly tickets to women.The party eventually fielded a large number of women candidates and also made promises aimed specifically at female voters, including smartphones for girls and electric scooters for female students. However, that move did not pay off. Congress won just two of the 403 assembly seats and its vote share slipped to around 2.3%.The situation, however, is different going into 2027. Congress won six Lok Sabha seats in Uttar Pradesh in 2024 as part of its alliance with the Samajwadi Party, which won 37. The opposition therefore enters the assembly battle with more political space than it had in 2022. For Congress, the challenge will be to revive its women outreach and aim to translate schemes into electoral benefit.But amid all the attention on cash transfers and the push for women-centric schemes, the question that remains is: Can women's votes be treated as one single bloc? A Jatav woman, a Muslim woman, a non-Yadav OBC woman may have very different expectations when she enters the polling booth to cast her vote. Caste, religion and past preferences may still continue to matter, as will factors like inflation, jobs, law and order, women's safety, welfare benefits and the candidate on the ground.Therefore, it is hard to predict if the high turnout among women can automatically translate into an advantage for any one party.But what it does surely mean is that no party can afford to take the 'Aadhi Aabadi' for granted anymore. When it comes to voting, women have outperformed men in the last three Uttar Pradesh assembly elections and have maintained that lead in the 2024 Lok Sabha polls as well. So, while caste will always play a role in UP elections, the 2027 battle will also come down to who wins the trust of the over six crore women voters. The question is no longer whether women will turn up to vote. It is: who will they vote for?
Article Summary: In Uttar Pradesh, 57.22% of women electors turned out to vote in the 2024 general elections, compared to 56.46% of men. In 2012, Uttar Pradesh had around 5.72 crore registered women voters, of whom 3.45 crore cast their ballots. By the 2017 assembly election, more than 4.09 crore women voted, and female turnout climbed to around 63.4%.

Article Title: 'Papa looking down proudly': Rahul, Priyanka's emotional note for 'Mama' Sonia Gandhi ahead of memoir release
Article Text:
Sonia Gandhi's memoir is scheduled to be released on November 10.

NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi and Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra on Thursday penned emotional notes for their mother Sonia Gandhi , who is set to release her memoir 'Belonging: A Journey of Love' in November.The messages came on the birth anniversary of their father, former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi, with both Rahul and Priyanka reflecting the relationship of their parents and the personal losses Sonia Gandhi endured over the years.Rahul, addressing his mother as 'Mama', recalled the last time he saw his parents together more than 35 years ago and spoke about Sonia Gandhi’s life after Rajiv Gandhi’s assassination in 1991."Mama, I last saw you and Papa together more than 35 years ago. Since the day Papa left, I have watched you face everything life threw at you with never-ending courage and dignity," Rahul wrote on X."Only Priyanka and I really know what you have been through, and how difficult your life after Papa truly was," he added.Rahul said he was proud that Sonia Gandhi, who has largely kept her personal life away from public view, had decided to tell her story."I am happy, and so proud, that your story 'Belonging: A Journey of Love' — will finally be read by the millions of people who love you. I know how hard it was for someone as private as you to tell the world your beautiful story," he wrote.Referring to Rajiv Gandhi’s birth anniversary, Rahul ended the note saying, "Today, on his birthday, I can see Papa smiling and looking down proudly at his beautiful Sonia."Priyanka Gandhi Vadra also shared a personal message, describing her parents’ relationship as "one of the greatest love stories of our time"."On my father’s birthday today, I think he would have been especially proud of my mother for having written her story with so much heart and honesty," she wrote.Priyanka said she felt privileged to have witnessed their relationship and hoped the memoir would allow readers to know Sonia Gandhi beyond her political persona."For me, it’s one of the greatest love stories of our time. I feel privileged to have witnessed it and I am happy that through her book, everyone will get to know my mother for what she truly is — a brave, loyal, compassionate woman, who is also tough as nails and great fun when she wants to be," she said.She described Sonia Gandhi as "a woman whose life has been a testament to her love for her husband and her country", before signing off: "Love you, ma and so, so proud of you."Sonia Gandhi’s memoir to release in NovemberPublisher Alfred A. Knopf announced earlier this week that Sonia Gandhi’s memoir, 'Belonging: A Journey of Love', will be published on November 10.The memoir traces her journey from her childhood in post-war Italy and her romance with Rajiv Gandhi during their time in Cambridge to her life in India and the personal tragedies that subsequently reshaped her life.Sonia Gandhi, 79, who remains the Congress’s longest-serving president, is also expected to revisit the assassinations of her mother-in-law and former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi and her husband Rajiv Gandhi.The book’s cover features a black-and-white photograph of Sonia Gandhi from her youth.Describing the memoir, the publisher said it tells a story of "love, family, and an endlessly fascinating country: India", adding that the "once famously reticent Sonia Gandhi opens up with warmth and candor" about her life.Born in Italy, Sonia Gandhi was a 19-year-old student in Cambridge when she met Rajiv Gandhi in 1965. The couple married on February 25, 1968.The memoir is scheduled to be released on November 10, 2026.
Article Summary: Sonia Gandhi's memoir is scheduled to be released on November 10. Leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi and Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra penned emotional notes for their mother. Sonia Gandhi is set to release her memoir 'Belonging: A Journey of Love' in November.

Article Title: How far will Jerry Jones go to punish Donovan Ezeiruaku? Cowboys’ $500K fine after Saints Brawl raises questions
Article Text:
How far will Jerry Jones go to punish Donovan Ezeiruaku? Cowboys’ $500K fine after Saints Brawl raises questions (Getty Images)

Jerry Jones confirms Donovan Ezeiruaku will face the Dallas Cowboys fine

Why Donovan Ezeiruaku’s second ejection has become a bigger concern?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Jerry Jones is not letting Donovan Ezeiruaku walk away from the Cowboys-Saints brawl without consequences. The Dallas Cowboys owner plans to appeal the team’s $500,000 NFL fine, but he has also confirmed that players involved in the fights will receive fines from Dallas.Ezeiruaku stands out because Jones indicated he will be among those players fined. The second-year linebacker was ejected after throwing a punch at Saints center Erik McCoy, making this more than just another heated training-camp moment.Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones has answered the biggest question surrounding Donovan Ezeiruaku. The Cowboys owner indicated that the young linebacker will receive a team fine after his role in the fight with New Orleans Saints center Erik McCoy.Jones spoke about the situation after the NFL fined the Cowboys and Saints $500,000 each for the repeated altercations during their joint practice. He made it clear that Dallas will handle the players separately from the league’s punishment.“I think that you have to have consequences, and that needs to register,” Jones said while speaking to reporters in Oxnard after the Cowboys completed their final training-camp practice there.He added that players need to understand the consequences of their behavior.That directly answers how far Jones plans to go with Ezeiruaku. The Cowboys will not simply accept the NFL fine and move forward. The team will also take money from the players responsible for the incidents.Jones has not announced the exact amount Ezeiruaku will pay. However, he indicated that Ezeiruaku is one of the Cowboys players who will receive a fine.The punishment comes after a chaotic joint practice that featured several fights between Dallas and New Orleans. Players from both sides exchanged punches, joined confrontations away from their original practice fields and pushed the session close to cancellation.The Cowboys and Saints coaches had to discuss whether they should end the practice early. Schottenheimer later said the session became too “chippy” and admitted that the teams did not get enough of the work they wanted.Ezeiruaku became one of the most visible Cowboys players in the chaos. He got into it with McCoy and threw a punch, leading officials to eject him.The bigger concern for Dallas is that this was his second ejection for throwing a punch during training camp. That makes the internal fine more than a simple response to one bad moment. The Cowboys now need Ezeiruaku to show that he can control his emotions while keeping the physical edge they want from him.Schottenheimer had already dealt with Ezeiruaku after his earlier ejection. The Cowboys coach again addressed the young defender after the Saints practice and stressed that Ezeiruaku cannot hurt the team by losing his composure.Speaking after the practice, Schottenheimer called Ezeiruaku a “very bright young man” and said he understands that he cannot hurt the football team. The coach also described the incident as part of a “growth mindset” and said Dallas has leaders who can help him improve.The message from Schottenheimer and Jones is similar. Dallas does not want to remove Ezeiruaku’s aggression. The Cowboys want him to know when that aggression has gone too far.That is especially important because Ezeiruaku has a meaningful role to play on the Dallas defense. He started nine games as a rookie and recorded two sacks, giving the Cowboys reason to continue developing him as part of their pass rush.The Cowboys therefore have no reason to give up on him over a pair of training-camp incidents. But they also cannot ignore repeated punches, especially when the latest incident helped turn a joint practice into a league disciplinary issue.The NFL fined Dallas and New Orleans $500,000 each after reviewing the fights. The league reminded teams that they must prevent unsportsmanlike behavior at joint practices, particularly conduct that could cause injuries.Jones called Dallas’ fine “pretty stiff” and said the Cowboys will appeal. He still understands why the league wants teams to control these situations.That creates two separate consequences for Ezeiruaku’s team. The Cowboys will challenge the $500,000 organizational fine, while Ezeiruaku and other players involved will pay separate fines to Dallas.The Cowboys have not revealed Ezeiruaku’s exact penalty. For now, Jones has made the main point clear: the linebacker will face a financial consequence, and the team expects him to learn from it.For Ezeiruaku, the next step is on the field. The Cowboys still want his physical style and pass-rush ability. They simply need him to keep his punches out of the equation.
Article Summary: Donovan Ezeiruaku will receive a team fine after his role in the fight with New Orleans Saints center Erik McCoy. The Cowboys owner indicated that the young linebacker will be one of the players fined. The NFL fined the Cowboys and Saints $500,000 each for the repeated altercations.

Article Title: Luka Doncic gives first Lakers roster outlook after spending $18,000 an hour flight for teammates: See Photos
Article Text:
Luka Doncic. Image via: Adam Pantozzi/ NBAE via Getty Images

Luka Doncic gives first Lakers roster outlook in LeBron James-less era

Luka Doncic shares a teammate's photo. Image via: Luka Doncic/ Instagram

Luka Doncic reportedly spent $18,000 an hour for teammates

The Lakers are building the roster around Doncic

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Luka Doncic has made his first major statement as the undisputed face of the Los Angeles Lakers. With LeBron James gone after joining the Philadelphia 76ers, Doncic brought the Lakers to Slovenia for a four-day minicamp designed to build chemistry before his first full season as the franchise's centerpiece. He welcomed his teammates with dinner, workouts, pickup games, golf and time exploring Ljubljana, turning an offseason trip into an early test of his leadership.The itinerary mixed basketball with leisure. The players worked out, played pickup games, visited Lake Bled for fishing, played golf and explored Ljubljana. Dinner at Doncic's favorite restaurant was also part of the trip.Doncic's Instagram Story captured the start of the gathering with a simple caption: “First supper,” Doncic wrote.The Lakers enter the 2026-27 season with Doncic at the center of everything. James' departure ended a defining chapter in Los Angeles, while Doncic's first full season as the team's unquestioned leader begins with a roster built around his offensive game.Doncic's production gives the Lakers plenty to build on. He led the league with 33.5 points per game in 2025-26 while averaging 8.3 assists, 7.7 rebounds and 1.6 steals.He shot 47.6% from the field and 36.6% from 3-point range.Los Angeles also made significant moves around him. The Lakers retained Austin Reaves on a four-year, $185 million contract and acquired Walker Kessler from the Utah Jazz through a sign-and-trade. Kessler received a four-year, $130 million deal, while the Lakers also sent two unprotected first-round picks and two first-round pick swaps in the transaction.Quentin Grimes, Collin Sexton, Sandro Mamukelashvili, Kevon Looney, Matisse Thybulle and Ziaire Williams were among the other additions. It appears that the Lakers are constructing a roster intended to maximize Doncic's strengths.The trip also came with a remarkable price tag. Doncic reportedly chartered a Bombardier Global 8000 for 14 Lakers players, with the 13-hour flight costing at least $18,000 per hour. The 26-hour round trip is expected to cost roughly $500,000, according to Slovenian outlet 24ur.com, with Doncic covering the expense.Doncic's leadership has not been limited to roster decisions. The Slovenia trip gave him a chance to create the kind of shared experience that can be difficult to manufacture during an NBA season.The 14 players reportedly traveled aboard a luxurious Bombardier Global 8000. Images from the flight showed a lounge area, individual bedrooms, beds, couches, recliners and televisions. After arriving, Doncic met his teammates alongside his daughter, Gabriela.The Lakers need their new hierarchy to work on the court, but Doncic also needs to establish himself inside a locker room that previously revolved around James.This is not Doncic's first attempt at bringing his teammates together. He organized a Porsche Driving Experience for the Lakers in October 2025, shortly after joining the organization.This minicamp carries more weight. James is no longer there, and Doncic now enters the season without another established superstar occupying the franchise's leadership role.The Lakers are also dealing with significant organizational change. Mark Walter's $12.5 billion purchase of the team and the Buss family's dispute over its remaining stakes have added another layer of uncertainty around the franchise.Doncic has so far handled that backdrop while remaining focused on basketball. The Slovenia minicamp gives him an opportunity to set the tone before training camp and the regular season arrive.
Article Summary: Luka Doncic took the Lakers to Slovenia for a four-day minicamp. The trip was designed to build chemistry before his first full season as the franchise's centerpiece. The itinerary mixed basketball with leisure, including fishing, golf and exploring Ljubljana.

Article Title: "I try to be the connector": Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry open up about their equal partnership in charity work
Article Text:

Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry explain how the two divide their work equally when it comes to their charity

Stephen Curry focuses on recovery amid concerns over his fitness ahead of the new season

Stephen Curry and his wife, Ayesha Curry, have always been a team even though their marriage has been surrounded by a number of negative rumors throughout the last decade. Despite the negative drama, Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry have remained united in all their efforts.A few weeks ago, in an interview with The Hollywood Reporter, Stephen Curry’s wife Ayesha Curry opened up about her work and department in their foundation, Eat. Play. Live, as she said, “I feel like I’m the big-ideas girl. I always have big, loud ideas that I want to accomplish now — or yesterday. The hardest thing for me, personally, has been reeling back a bit to come to the understanding that baby steps are important. ”The four time NBA champion Stephen Curry also opened up about his area of work as he added, “I try to be the connector, especially when we’re reaching out to our network. We’re building a family, in a sense, of people who, again, believe in our mission and want to commit time and resources, whether that be financial or otherwise.”The Golden State Warriors’ star player continued, “When I’m on the court, I want people to enjoy the way that I played…I want them to feel something and be inspired to achieve greatness in whatever they decide to do.Family-wise, we want to have a cohort of hopefully thousands of kids whose lives have been impacted because of the work that we’ve done. We don’t need a parade for that. It’s who we are.”Both the four time NBA champion Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry have remained dedicated towards building their foundation, Eat. Learn and Play, throughout the last decade.Eat. Learn and Play has actively worked for underprivileged children and families in Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry’s hometown, Oakland.Throughout the last decade, the team has actively worked for over 10,000 children and has looked after their food and provided quality education.Both Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry have handled their busy professional and personal lives while they have actively worked towards the children in Oakland.Ahead of the new season, there have been many concerns about Stephen Curry’s fitness after he ended up sustaining a patellofemoral pain syndrome (runner's knee) and bone bruising in his right knee which kept him out of court for two months.Even though the NBA legend could come back for his team, Stephen Curry has kept his full focus on complete recovery during the offseason.With the Golden State Warriors scheduled to play a demanding season, many remain stressed about him.
Article Summary: Stephen Curry and his wife, Ayesha Curry, have always been a team even though their marriage has been surrounded by a number of negative rumors throughout the last decade. A 16-year-old girl is facing assault and disorderly conduct charges after she ran onto the field during a middle school football game in Winchester, Tennessee, and tackled a South Middle School player. The incident happened Tuesday night during the game against Cornersville Middle School at Franklin County High School. Game officials stopped the game and the stadium was cleared. No injuries were reported, according to WSMV and the Franklin County Sheriff’s Office.The incident began after South Middle School scored a touchdown and an extra point. According to WSMV, a scuffle then started between two players from the teams. Investigators said the 16-year-old girl, who is from Marshall County, ran onto the field and went straight toward the South Middle School player involved in that exchange.Video from the game shows the girl coming from the stands and making contact with the player, sending both to the ground. The player got back up, but the girl pushed him down again. A person who appeared to be a coach then stepped in and stopped the confrontation.The girl left the field afterward, but a school resource officer met her as she was leaving. She was later released to her parents, who were at the game. The Franklin County Sheriff’s Office said she was charged with assault and disorderly conduct.The reason she ran onto the field has not been confirmed by authorities. Reports only connect her actions to the scuffle that followed South Middle School’s touchdown. There is no official information showing what, if anything, happened between the girl and the player before she entered the field.Referees ended the game after the girl entered the field. Officials cleared the playing area and then emptied the stadium. The game between South Middle School and Cornersville Middle School did not continue.NewsChannel 5 reported that no one was injured in the incident. The Franklin County Sheriff’s Office also confirmed that the girl was released to her parents after she was taken into custody.The school consequences are also serious. Franklin County Schools issued a lifetime ban keeping the girl off all district properties. The Tennessee Secondary School Athletic Association separately banned her from attending Cornersville Middle School home and away athletic events for one year.The game was played at Franklin County High School because South uses that venue for home games. The Tennessee Secondary School Athletic Association confirmed the one-year event ban. The incident was captured on video and circulated in reports about the game.WSMV reported that South Middle School’s principal praised the staff, coaches and school resource officers for how they handled the situation.The girl’s identity has not been made public because she is 16. The available reports do not say whether she has a lawyer or give further details about the juvenile case. Authorities have not publicly stated what led to the confrontation beyond the scuffle involving the players.

Article Title: Inspiring story on motherhood: "It's probably the hardest thing I've ever done in my life...it's the most daunting task" - How Donna Kelce navigated the challenges of raising Jason and Travis Kelce
Article Text:
Jason Kelce, Donna Kelce and Travis Kelce (Getty Images)

Donna Kelce’s powerful words about motherhood

Glamour group interview published on October 3, 2024

Raising Jason and Travis Kelce was never just about football

Donna Kelce was also building a career

The values behind Jason and Travis Kelce’s success

Why Donna Kelce’s motherhood confession still resonates

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

For Donna Kelce, motherhood was never simply about getting her children through childhood. It meant working hard, making difficult choices and giving Jason and Travis Kelce the freedom to discover who they were. Years before they became NFL stars, she was a working mother trying to keep family life steady. In 2024, she opened up about just how demanding that journey had been.Donna Kelce shared her candid thoughts on motherhood during a. The conversation was part of Glamour’s 2024 Women of the Year feature, which brought together Donna, Tina Knowles, Maggie Baird and Mandy Teefey to discuss raising children who would eventually become major figures in sports, music and entertainment.Asked about what motherhood had been like for her, Donna did not describe it as an effortless or glamorous experience. Instead, she focused on the responsibility that comes with raising children who depend on you for almost everything.She said:“Being a mom is probably the hardest thing I’ve ever done in my life. It’s so much easier to just go to work.”Donna Kelce then explained that raising children means trying to make the best choices possible while dealing with limited resources and the constant responsibility of caring for people who rely on you.She ultimately described motherhood as the most daunting task she had ever taken on.The honesty in her answer is striking because it came from someone whose sons would later become two of the most recognizable names in American football. Yet Donna was not talking about fame when she made the comment. She was talking about the everyday work of being a mother.That distinction matters.Jason and Travis Kelce did not begin their childhoods with a clear path toward professional football. Donna told Glamour that the brothers tried several sports, including hockey, lacrosse and basketball. Football came later, when they reached seventh grade.Even then, Donna did not immediately know that her sons would build professional careers from the sport.She said the possibility became clearer only when college recruiting letters began arriving. Until that point, she was simply watching two athletic boys grow, compete and find interests of their own.That detail gives her motherhood comments more weight.The woman who eventually became known around the NFL as “Mama Kelce” was not raising two guaranteed stars. She was raising children without knowing where their talents would eventually take them. Her job was to give them room to grow while keeping them grounded.Donna has also spoken about the energetic nature of her sons as children. During the same Glamour conversation, she recalled broken windows and calls from neighbors, while making clear that Jason and Travis were not bad children. They were simply energetic and, as she put it, rambunctious.Those memories offer a very different picture from the polished image fans now see.Before the Super Bowl appearances, championship celebrations and packed stadiums, there were ordinary family moments. There were mistakes, sports practices, neighborhood adventures and the countless small responsibilities that come with raising children.Another important part of Donna’s story is that motherhood did not happen in isolation.She was also working.Donna had a career in banking and later described herself as a major breadwinner in her family. She told Glamour that she worked extremely hard because she wanted to move forward professionally. At the same time, she believed it was important for her children to see that a woman could build a career and pursue her own ambitions.That balance adds another layer to her comments about motherhood.For Donna, going to work could be demanding, but parenting carried a different kind of responsibility. A job has defined duties, deadlines and hours. Raising children is far less predictable. It follows you home. It changes as children grow. And there is no simple measure for whether you are doing it right.Her reflections also touched on her marriage to Ed Kelce. Donna said the couple knew their marriage was no longer working but chose to remain together for their children for a period of time. She described their relationship as friendly and said they wanted to keep life as normal as possible for Jason and Travis.Eventually, Donna said she had to move forward on her own.That part of her story shows that her definition of motherhood was not limited to the visible moments. It included personal sacrifices and decisions that her sons may not have fully understood while they were growing up.Donna Kelce’s influence becomes easier to understand when looking at how she talks about her sons today.She has consistently emphasized supporting children rather than forcing them into a particular future. In the Glamour interview, she explained that parents learn more about their children as they encounter people and experiences outside their immediate community. Her approach was to support what her children loved and encourage them to enjoy it.That philosophy appears to have shaped the Kelce family.Jason eventually became a Super Bowl champion with the Philadelphia Eagles and one of the most respected centers of his generation. Travis established himself as one of the NFL’s premier tight ends with the Kansas City Chiefs.Their achievements are enormous. But Donna's comments suggest that she measures success differently.For her, keeping her sons grounded mattered just as much as celebrating their accomplishments.She told Glamour that she would remind Jason and Travis of their childhood when fame became overwhelming. The goal was simple: remind them where they came from and help them remember that they were still the same people they had always been.That perspective became especially meaningful as both brothers entered a world where almost every part of their lives could attract public attention.Donna Kelce’s description of motherhood stands out because it cuts through the glamour surrounding her family.Today, Jason and Travis are household names. Their games attract millions of viewers, their personal lives generate constant headlines and their family has become part of the wider sports conversation.But Donna’s story began somewhere much quieter.It began with a mother working, raising two boys and trying to make good decisions without knowing exactly where those decisions would lead.Her statement to Glamour was powerful because she did not present motherhood as a perfect journey. She acknowledged the pressure, uncertainty and sacrifice involved. She also recognized that the work of raising children often happens without applause.That may be the most revealing part of her story.The world sees the Super Bowl rings, the records and the stadium lights. Donna remembers the years before all of that. She remembers the children who needed her, the choices she had to make and the effort required to help them become independent adults.Her famous sons may now be the stars, but Donna’s words offer a reminder that behind many extraordinary careers is a much more ordinary story: a parent showing up, day after day, and doing the best they can.And for Donna Kelce, that was the hardest job of all.
Article Summary: Jason and Travis Kelce's mother, Donna Kelce, opened up about motherhood in 2024. She said it was the most daunting task she had ever taken on. Donna did not immediately know that her sons would build professional careers from the sport.

Article Title: After Jaspal Rana’s sudden demise, Paris Olympic medallist Manu Bhaker forging new bonds with Serbian coach
Article Text:
Manu Bhaker with her new coach (Photo by Jelena Arunovic)

BHOPAL: After adjusting the lighting at the MP State Shooting Academy final hall, two young electricians asked Manu Bhaker if she needed anything else. “Nahin,” the shooting star politely replied. The electricians were still waiting. Distracted, Manu suddenly realized it hadn’t hit home, and gave them a thumbs up with a smile.Job well done, the men left the range content.With that stardom and popularity that surrounds her, the Paris Olympics double medallist may have realised at that moment, that a lot rides on her validation.Nearly a decade ago, in 2017, Manu, already a teenage star, was known to getting things done her way. Calling it stubbornness would perhaps be much; insistence on her plans, especially those concerning her sport, was her weapon. It was also the reason for her success.She has a different weapon now -- flexibility. While a certain doggedness suited her teenage self, flexibility is becoming of a mature Manu.Other than being a good judge of situations, Manu is also mastering the art of changing according to its demands.After the sudden passing away of her coach, Jaspal Rana, two months back, Manu has adapted herself with Serbian coach Jelena Arunovic.The Indian star, attending the Asian Games camp here, has been spending over eight hours at the ranges. She reaches the range at 7.30 am and is the last to leave with Jelena late afternoon. In between, some intense training happens.“Her openness to new methodologies has definitely made the transition to a slightly different way of working easier,” Jelena told TOI.“I think her flexibility comes first from the fact that she is never completely satisfied with her current level. She is always looking for what can still be improved, either to achieve a better result or to make her performance more stable. That is actually a trait of top athletes,” she added.The shooter is forging a bond with her new coach, spends hours with her at the ranges, and follows the unconventional ways of training that the Serbian brings. The 24-year-old does all this, without fuss or frown.“I think flexibility at this level does not mean accepting every change immediately. It means being able to understand why something is being changed, test it seriously, and then see whether it can actually help your performance,” Jelena, who had coached her sister Zorana to a gold in Paris, said.It isn’t just about training under a new coach. It is also about training with different ideas and different philosophies. With less than two years left for the 2028 LA Games, the star of 2024 looks in no mood for complacency. She rather looks hungry for more and is doing everything to repeat her performance.
Article Summary: Manu Bhaker has adapted herself with Serbian coach Jelena Arunovic. The shooter is forging a bond with her new coach, spends hours with her at the ranges. With less than two years left for the 2028 LA Games, the star of 2024 looks hungry for more.

Article Title: Why referees are banned from speaking on TV at Real Madrid’s stadium despite La Liga’s new transparency protocol
Article Text:
Real Madrid president Florentino Perez gives a press conference in Madrid, Tuesday, May 12, 2026. (AP Photo/Bernat Armangue)

What is La Liga's new refereeing protocol?

Referee shows a yellow card to Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe during a Spanish La Liga soccer match between Real Madrid and Girona in Madrid, Spain, Friday, April 10, 2026. (AP Photo/Manu Fernandez)

Why is the Bernabéu the exception?

A problem rooted in Real Madrid's tense relationship with La Liga

What will fans see elsewhere?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

La Liga has introduced a new refereeing protocol designed to give supporters more insight into how key decisions are made, with officials now able to speak on television about important incidents. But there is one notable exception to the new system: Real Madrid’s Santiago Bernabéu.Referees will be able to give pre-match and post-match interviews at La Liga stadiums when requested by broadcasters, as well as explain the most significant decisions and incidents from games. The Bernabéu is the only one of La Liga’s 20 stadiums where the protocol cannot be used, because Real Madrid’s restrictions on broadcasters’ connections prevent the interviews from taking place. At every other venue, referees will be available to speak before and after matches.The policy marks a significant change from the traditional approach of referees remaining largely silent when it comes to explaining their decisions.The first referee interventions were heard during the opening round of La Liga, while the system is due to expand from Matchday 10. From that point, referees will be able to speak before and after matches when broadcasters request interviews, and they can also be asked about the most notable incidents from the game.The Spanish refereeing body has stressed that officials will speak in stadiums “where the necessary conditions for this are available”, while insisting there is no distinction between clubs or grounds.That means the intention is for supporters around Spain to hear referees explain some of the decisions that can otherwise leave fans debating what happened and why.The Santiago Bernabéu is the only La Liga stadium excluded from the new system, according to Catalan newspaper Sport The reason is not that the refereeing committee has specifically banned Real Madrid from participating, nor is there a separate rule targeting the club. Instead, it comes down to the broadcasting arrangements at the stadium.Real Madrid restricts broadcasters' connections from the Bernabéu, allowing them to be established only a few minutes before kick-off. Those restrictions prevent broadcasters from creating the connections needed for the referee interviews to take place under the new protocol.In practical terms, referees can speak at other stadiums because the necessary broadcast infrastructure and connections can be arranged. At the Bernabéu, the existing restrictions make that impossible.The broadcasting restrictions come against the backdrop of an already strained relationship between Real Madrid and both La Liga and the Spanish Football Federation (RFEF).That tension has also affected the conditions under which broadcasters operate from the Bernabéu. Real Madrid, under president Florentino Pérez, maintains restrictions on when broadcasters can establish their connections from the stadium, and those conditions now have a direct impact on the new refereeing transparency initiative.The refereeing body has made clear that this is not a decision by its officials to exclude Real Madrid. Its position is that referees will speak wherever the required conditions exist and that there is no discrimination between clubs or stadiums.From Matchday 10 onwards, supporters at other La Liga grounds will be able to hear referees speak before and after matches when broadcasters request their participation. Officials will also be able to explain the most important decisions and incidents from the game.The measure is intended to provide greater transparency around refereeing decisions and give supporters a better understanding of why officials reached particular conclusions.The Bernabéu, however, will remain outside that system.So while the rest of La Liga moves towards giving fans more direct access to referees and their explanations, Real Madrid's home supporters will not have the same opportunity at their own stadium — not because referees have been instructed to stay silent there, but because of the broadcasting restrictions already in place at the Bernabéu.
Article Summary: La Liga has introduced a new refereeing protocol to give supporters more insight into how key decisions are made. But there is one notable exception to the new system: Real Madrid’s Santiago Bernabéu. Referees will be able to give pre-match and post-match interviews at La Liga stadiums when requested by broadcasters. At every other venue, referees will be available to speak before and after matches. But Real Madrid's restrictions on broadcasters' connections prevent the interviews from taking place.

Article Title: Joe Root scripts history, becomes first player to achieve this feat

Joe Root etched his name into the World Test Championship record books on Friday, becoming the first player to score 3,000 runs as a captain in the WTC during England’s opening Test against Pakistan at Headingley in Leeds.Root needed 42 runs to reach the landmark at the start of the match and completed the milestone in the second session of Day 2. The Yorkshire batter had resumed the day unbeaten on 37 after England reached 112-2 on a rain-affected opening day. He added the remaining five runs after lunch to bring up 3,000 WTC runs as captain.The 35-year-old returned to the England captaincy following Ben Stokes’ retirement from international cricket in June 2026. His latest achievement further underlined his consistency in the longest format, with Root now having 3,000 runs from 34 matches and 63 innings as WTC captain. He has scored eight centuries and 13 fifties, with a highest score of 228, while averaging 50.13.Root is comfortably ahead of the leading run-scorers in the WTC as captain. Former England skipper Stokes occupies second place with 2,182 runs from 40 matches, followed by Sri Lanka’s Dimuth Karunaratne on 2,160.West Indies captain Kraigg Brathwaite has 1,994 runs, while Pakistan’s Babar Azam has 1,918.Root’s milestone came during another strong batting display from England, who ended Day 2 on 366-8, taking a first-innings lead of 195 runs over Pakistan.Root scored 66 and played a key role in a 150-run partnership with Jordan Cox, who made 73. Harry Brook narrowly missed out on a century, falling for 91 at his home ground. Dan Lawrence, playing his first Test in two years, also contributed with a 51.Pakistan’s Ali Usman was the standout bowler, claiming 5-92 for his first five-wicket haul in Test cricket.The visitors had been dismissed for just 171 on the opening day, leaving England firmly in control of the first Test. Pakistan’s bowling and fielding also came under scrutiny as England’s batters capitalised on several opportunities to build a substantial lead.For Root, however, the focus was on another landmark in a Test career that continues to produce records. His 3,000 WTC runs as captain put him alone at the top of the tournament’s captaincy batting charts.
Article Summary: Joe Root becomes the first player to score 3,000 runs as a captain in the WTC during England’s opening Test against Pakistan at Headingley in Leeds. Former England fast bowler Stuart Broad has delivered a blunt verdict on Pakistan, describing them as a "poor side" and backing England to complete a 3-0 clean sweep in the three-Test series.Speaking on The Love for Cricket Podcast, Broad was critical of Pakistan's current Test team and suggested England should be expected to dominate the series."They are a poor side, they are not a really good side. He added that failing to win the series would represent a major disappointment for the hosts."But that isn't guaranteed. Pakistan were bowled out for just 171 on the opening day, with England's bowlers exposing the tourists' batting problems.England then took firm control with the bat, reaching 366-8 by stumps on Day 2 to secure a 195-run first-innings lead.Joe Root and Harry Brook were among four England batters to register half-centuries.Root made 66 and shared a 150-run partnership with Jordan Cox, who scored 73, while Dan Lawrence contributed 51 on his return to Test cricket after two years.Brook, meanwhile, narrowly missed out on a century at his home ground. The world's top-ranked Test batter made 91 after surviving an early scare when he was dropped on one. Article Title: Bichu Devi’s stunning save helps India hold England, reach World Cup next round

With just about half a minute left for the hooter, England’s Tessa Howard fired a shot of strange menace and intent towards the right side of the Indian goal — on the turn, and from the edge of the D.Hearts stopped for that moment, and some, as the ball flew as if in slow motion towards the Indian goal. Actually, it was whizzing in at the speed of light, a silent scream that would quell all the support the stands had drummed up, and all the hope that India had harboured.Up until then — for 59 minutes and 30 seconds — India had defended with everything they had. They had kept England — needing a win to make it to the next round of the World Cup at Amstelveen’s Wagener Stadium — from finding the back of the net. But for that split second, it seemed England had done it.Almost out of nowhere, Bichu Devi Kharibam dived to her left and magnificently kept out the ball with her walrus-sized paws to deny England a terrific — and certain — goal. The goalkeeper from Manipur, who had dreamt of playing football as a child, had made one of the biggest saves of her career, and for Indian women’s hockey.You could actually see the England players physically deflate.Devastated, all they could do was helplessly watch the clock run out as the match ended in a goalless draw.It was all India needed to make it to the next round, and the entire team achieved it by playing out a draw that was high on stress for most of the hour as it was on defensive organisation.“We fought for everything. We were really good as a team, especially in defence!” captain Salima Tete, who was sensational with her rushing during the many penalty corners that England won, was understandably ecstatic afterwards.England had 11 penalty corners, 20 shots on goal, 19 circle entries and 52.4% possession. Despite their domination, India prevailed, thanks to their calm and disciplined approach.They did give the ball away cheaply in the middle, but they held their ground when it mattered most. The seniors, especially Nikki Pradhan, Navneet Kaur, Neha Goyal and Sushila Chanu, not only did well individually but also marshalled the team effectively.“England are good, but we just decided that until the last second, we would not stop. We kept fighting and kept going,” said the captain. “England are good at attacking penalty corners, but we defended well. So, credit to our defence.”With achieving the stalemate that they had planned for, India got the one point they needed and made it out of Pool D in second place with five points from four matches. China, who beat South Africa 5-1 earlier in the day, finished on top with seven points. Both will now enter Pool E along with the top two teams from Pool A — Netherlands and Australia.India will next face hosts Netherlands on Friday. It poses a hugely difficult challenge, and India will have to convert their chances — something they just couldn’t do against England.At half-time, India had won four penalty corners but couldn’t convert any, a point that will worry coach Sjoerd Marijne ahead of the encounter against the world No. 1 side.Speaking at half-time, he had said: “We get enough penalty corners, but we have to be more precise with the injection. If we do that better, I think we can score some goals.”Credit should also go to England goalkeeper Miriam Pritchard, who made some breathtaking saves to keep India at bay. In the end, England pulled her out to play an extra outfield player, but India held on.India, though, don’t have much time to celebrate. They will have to regroup quickly and prepare for one of the most difficult tasks in world hockey — facing Netherlands, the reigning world and Olympic champions, and that too in front of the Dutch fans.
Article Summary: India held to a goalless draw by England in their final Pool D match. India will now face hosts Netherlands in the next round of the World Cup. England had 11 penalty corners, 20 shots on goal, 19 circle entries and 52.4% possession.

Article Title: Losses, betting probe, corruption: BCB suspends Bangladesh Premier League after years of chaos
Article Text:
Bangladesh cricket team players (left), and BCB

Bangladesh’s top domestic T20 tournament, the Bangladesh Premier League (BPL), will not be held this year as the Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) plans to restructure the competition, board president Tamim Iqbal said on Thursday.Tamim said the tournament has been suspended because several franchises failed to follow the league’s rules and regulations."The BPL will not happen this year," Tamim told reporters.The BPL began in 2012 and is Bangladesh’s biggest domestic cricket tournament. However, it has struggled to match the success of franchise leagues in countries such as India and Australia.Tamim said the BCB has also been dealing with unpaid dues and problems related to bank guarantees. According to him, the board has lost around $3.3 million from the BPL over the past two years."The BPL is a great product and there is a lot of interest in it. If we can do it properly, the interest will increase even more," Tamim said."BCB is supposed to make a profit from franchise cricket, not a loss. So until we fix this, holding a tournament at a loss is not important," he said.Bangladeshi newspaper Prothom Alo reported that the BCB suffered losses of nearly 400 million Bangladeshi taka ($3.27 million) during the last two BPL seasons.Tamim said he understood the disappointment among players but believes rebuilding the tournament is more important."If I was a player, I'd be disheartened too," Tamim added."But they also know that this tournament should be staged in a way that the BCB can be proud of. Are we proud of what has happened over the last few years? Perhaps not."The BPL has faced several issues in recent months. In May, the BCB suspended a player and multiple team officials over betting violations after an anti-corruption investigation into the tournament.The previous season also saw several matches rescheduled after domestic cricketers boycotted games over comments made by BCB official Nazmul Islam, who criticised players and questioned their financial value.Tamim said the BCB is committed to bringing the tournament back but will take time to fix the problems."Our intention is 1,000 percent to host BPL. But I do not want to rush. I want to do it properly; if it takes six months or 12 months, I will take that time," he added.Tamim, who was recently appointed chairman of the International Cricket Council’s new Franchise League Committee, said Bangladesh’s experience with the BPL makes the overhaul even more important."If franchise cricket does not run properly in my country, then stopping it, and rebuilding it, will be a big message for my committee," he said.Tamim made the announcement while launching the Game Development (GD) Trophy, a new tournament featuring Bangladesh’s under-17, under-19 and under-23 teams.He added that the BCB has started discussions with existing franchises and plans to complete the franchise selection process by April or May next year. The board is also open to including foreign franchises in the revamped BPL.
Article Summary: Bangladesh's top domestic T20 tournament, the Bangladesh Premier League (BPL), will not be held this year. The Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) plans to restructure the competition. The BPL has struggled to match the success of franchise leagues in countries such as India and Australia.

Article Title: Joe Root equals Sachin Tendulkar’s record for most fifties in Test cricket
Article Text:

Most fifties in Tests

Root, Cox put England in command

Joe Root added another landmark to his extraordinary Test career on Thursday, equalling Indian batting legend Sachin Tendulkar’s record for the most half-centuries in Test cricket during England’s first Test against Pakistan at Headingley.Root brought up his 68th Test fifty on the second day before being dismissed for 66 off 112 balls, including 10 boundaries. The milestone put the England captain level with Tendulkar at the top of the all-time list for most fifties in the longest format.West Indies batter Shivnarine Chanderpaul is third on the list with 66, while former Australia captain Allan Border and India great Rahul Dravid have 63 each. Ricky Ponting is next with 62.For Root, the achievement came on a significant day in his international career as he returned to the England Test captaincy following Ben Stokes' retirement.Root resumed the day alongside Jordan Cox with England on 112/2, still 59 runs behind Pakistan’s first-innings total of 171. The pair proceeded to take control of the contest, putting together a century partnership that carried England beyond Pakistan’s modest total.Cox was the more aggressive of the two initially and went on to score 73 before being dismissed by Ali Usman. Root followed soon afterwards, falling for 66 as Pakistan finally broke through after the drinks interval.Khurram Shahzad trapped Root lbw with an inswinger that moved back sharply. Root shuffled down the pitch looking to work the ball away but failed to make contact, with the delivery striking him in front of middle stump.The dismissal also left England without any reviews.Root’s 66 ensured that his 68th fifty came without a century, but the milestone further underlined his remarkable consistency in Test cricket. His tally of 68 fifties now matches Tendulkar’s record, with Root having the opportunity to move outright clear at the top in his next innings.Root has also climbed into the top five for most 50-plus scores as a Test captain, with his latest half-century taking his tally to 42 in that category. South Africa’s Graeme Smith leads the list with 61, followed by Ponting (54), Border (51) and Pakistan’s Misbah-ul-Haq (43).England had earlier put themselves in a strong position by bowling Pakistan out for just 171 after Root won the toss and opted to field in favourable conditions.Ollie Robinson and Josh Tongue shared the wickets, taking five apiece. Robinson finished with figures of 5/51, while Tongue returned 5/46 as Pakistan’s batting line-up struggled against England’s pace attack.Abdullah Shafique provided the main resistance for Pakistan, scoring 61, but England kept the pressure on and eventually dismissed the visitors inside 49 overs.
Article Summary: Joe Root equals Sachin Tendulkar's record for most fifties in Test cricket. England captain scores 68th Test fifty before being dismissed for 66. Root has also climbed into the top five for most 50-plus scores as a Test captain, with his latest half-century taking his tally to 42.

Article Title: NHL Trade Rumors: Cutter Gauthier camp rejects Anaheim Ducks contract offer as Pavel Zacha's Boston Bruins future remains uncertain

Will Pavel Zacha stay with the Boston Bruins or become a trade candidate?

The Anaheim Ducks and Boston Bruins are facing two contract situations that could shape their plans for the upcoming NHL season. Cutter Gauthier is coming off a breakout year in Anaheim, while Pavel Zacha is entering the final season of his current deal in Boston.Both players have reasons to attract attention around the league. Gauthier has put himself in a strong position after his latest season, while Zacha’s future could become a bigger talking point as the Bruins weigh their options before the trade deadline.Gauthier is coming off his entry-level contract after scoring 41 goals and 69 points last season. The 21-year-old winger does not have arbitration rights and also cannot sign an offer sheet because he has not played enough NHL games to qualify. That normally would give Anaheim more control in contract talks. However, Gauthier’s production gives him a strong reason to ask for a much bigger deal.On Sunday, NHL Network Radio’s Paul Shaheen said reliable sources told him that Gauthier’s camp rejected a four-year contract worth an average annual value of $13 million. Shaheen also said the Ducks may need to get creative with their salary cap situation if and when Gauthier signs.The problem comes from Leo Carlsson’s new contract. Anaheim matched the Philadelphia Flyers’ five-year, $90 million offer sheet for Carlsson last month, giving him an $18 million annual average value. According to PuckPedia, the Ducks have just over $9 million in cap space, making it difficult to sign a new deal for Gauthier without moving salary.Sportsnet’s Emily Sadler also pointed to the cap issue. Anaheim will get some relief next summer when Chris Kreider and Alex Killorn become unrestricted free agents, but the Ducks still have to find a way to fit Gauthier into their current plans.The situation around Pavel Zacha is different, but his future in Boston is also worth watching. The 29-year-old center is entering the final season of his four-year contract, which carries a $4.75 million AAV. Unless he signs an extension, he will become an unrestricted free agent next July.Boston Herald’s Steve Conroy believes Zacha has been a reliable player for Boston and could still have a place on the team. However, his trade value may be higher than ever, which could give the Bruins another option. There is another factor for Boston to consider. Re-signing Zacha could make it harder for young centers such as Fraser Minten, James Hagens or Dean Letourneau to move into bigger roles.The Bruins are believed to want Zacha back, but he was also part of trade speculation earlier this offseason. Conroy noted that Boston is unlikely to move him without getting a deal done before the season begins. His situation could become more interesting around the March 1 trade deadline if the Bruins are out of playoff contention.For now, Anaheim needs to solve its cap situation before getting Gauthier signed, while Boston must decide whether Zacha is part of its long-term plans or could become a valuable trade piece.
Article Summary: The Anaheim Ducks and Boston Bruins are facing two contract situations that could shape their plans for the upcoming NHL season. Cutter Gauthier is coming off a breakout year in Anaheim, while Pavel Zacha is entering the final season of his current deal in Boston. Zacha's future could become a bigger talking point as the Bruins weigh their options.

Article Title: Valkyrae’s AI controversy grows as streamer reveals the artist behind her disputed YouTube thumbnail
Article Text:
Valkyrae addresses AI allegations over YouTube thumbnail

Valkyrae defends thumbnail artist Anko

Rachell “Valkyrae” Hofstetter has addressed a growing debate over the artwork used for her YouTube livestreams after viewers accused her latest thumbnail of being AI-generated. The streamer defended her longtime thumbnail artist, Anko, while admitting she understands why some people reached that conclusion. Her comments also highlight a wider concern for digital artists as AI-generated content continues to reshape how audiences view online artwork.The controversy began after Anko, Valkyrae’s thumbnail artist, shared the creative process behind artwork for her Uncharted playthrough. The thumbnail initially received attention from viewers, but some quickly questioned whether artificial intelligence had been used to create it.That reaction eventually reached Valkyrae, who explained that Anko creates all of her YouTube livestream thumbnails and regularly shares his process online. She also pointed out the irony of the situation, saying that even those behind-the-scenes videos have not stopped people from making AI accusations.Valkyrae said:"Okay. We have to talk about this thumbnail debacle. I don't know what to do about this thumbnail debacle.So, as most of you know, every single one of my YouTube livestream thumbnails is made by the same artist. His name is Anko, and he makes all of them. He even posts on Twitter the art process of making them, but it still never beats the AI allegations. And the most recent thumbnail, he makes new thumbnails when I start a new game series, so, obviously, there is a new thumbnail for the Uncharted era. And people were saying, 'Oh, it's AI slop,' in the pre-chat."The streamer then offered a more nuanced response. Rather than dismissing viewers who suspected AI, she said she understood where their reaction came from. At the same time, she wanted to make clear that the artwork was not created using AI.Valkyrae added:"'Just ignore them.' Well, no. Okay? I don't blame people for thinking it's AI because AI is using people's art, like Anko's, to take over. But I would like to clear it up because there were a few people that were saying, 'Oh! When I saw the thumb, I also thought it was AI.' So now I am wondering how many people are out there that would watch the stream, but didn't because of the AI-looking thumbnail! But it's not AI."The discussion also became personal for Valkyrae because she said she felt bad for Anko. The thumbnail was later updated, with the artist adding his signature, giving viewers another indication of who created the work.Valkyrae explained that the situation made her think about the broader impact AI tools could have on working artists. For creators who depend on commissioned digital artwork, being mistaken for AI-generated work can create a difficult problem. The visual style that once helped an artist stand out can now cause audiences to question whether a human created it at all.She said:"I don't know, dude. I don't know what to do about it. I feel bad for him, though, because... and then, it, like, reminded me. I was like, 'Man, I just shouldn't do art thumbnails.' But then, the whole AI thing is doing what it does - making artists lose their jobs! Isn't that crazy?!"The controversy has now become more than a discussion about one YouTube thumbnail. Valkyrae’s response reflects a growing tension between AI-generated imagery and human-made digital art, particularly on social media where polished artwork can be judged within seconds.For Valkyrae, however, the message is straightforward: the Uncharted thumbnail was made by Anko, not AI. The debate instead shows how difficult it has become for artists to prove the human work behind their creations.
Article Summary: Valkyrae defends thumbnail artist Anko after viewers accuse him of being AI- generated. The streamer says she understands where people are coming from, but wants to make clear that the artwork was not created using AI. The debate shows how difficult it has become for artists to prove the human work behind their creations.

Article Title: "I'm grateful for every lesson": Gisele Bündchen’s candid Tom Brady divorce admission revealed the pain behind her new beginning
Article Text:

Gisele Bündchen opens up about Tom Brady divorce

Gisele Bündchen focuses on her children after divorce
